definition: Appalling means causing shock, horror, or disgust.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word appalling. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know appalling should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The star's appalling behavior at the awards banquet — mocking the hosts, tipping over a chair — cost him three sponsors by morning.
Disappointing is far milder than appalling — the results merely fell short of hopes, and everyone sighs and moves on; nothing here turns a stomach.
Monstrous goes further than appalling — appalling conditions disgust whoever reads the report; monstrous cruelty makes them question the humanity of whoever caused it.

Shocking covers the jolt of pure surprise — a result no one saw coming — and stops there. Appalling goes past surprise into moral disgust: the sight is not just startling but a disgrace to look at. News can be shocking without anyone being at fault; appalling says the thing itself is shameful.

Dreadful is loose, all-purpose badness — dreadful weather, a dreadful commute — with no verdict attached. Appalling is specific and moral: what you are looking at shocks and disgusts, and someone is answerable for it. Dreadful complains; appalling condemns.

The stories printed that week called the whole scene appalling, and enlistment in the port towns fell by half.
Appalling is the exact word for such a scene, because it means causing shock, horror, or disgust — the sight does not merely surprise you; it turns your stomach and drains the color from your face.

In 1908 the photographer Lewis Hine began slipping into coal towns with a hidden agenda and a camera.
What he recorded was appalling: boys of eight and nine hunched over coal chutes ten hours a day, their fingers bleeding from sorting rock, their lungs full of dust.
Mine owners knew the boys' ages.
Paymasters wrote false birth dates into the ledgers, and inspectors were steered past the breaker rooms.
Hine's photographs left viewers no room to look away, and no one to excuse.
The shame belonged to the men who profited.
Within a decade, the pictures had done what pamphlets could not, and the first serious child labor laws began to pass.
